description: CPU Hartree-Fock through the libcint backend. Reference energies are PySCF RHF on the same geometry and basis, not values this program produced -- a manifest of its own output would only detect change, not error. Kept separate from validation_tests.json because that one is xTB and needs tblite, while these need libcint and nothing else. The 6-31G* pair is the Cartesian case. 6-31G* specifies six d functions and Basis Set Exchange marks them so; reading them as five, which is what this program did until the reader learned to look at function_type, gives -76.008427 in 18 functions instead of -76.009809 in 19. Both converge, and only one of them is 6-31G*. These two references were generated by feeding PySCF the exponents and coefficients out of basis_sets/6-31g_st_.json rather than its own basis tables: BSE writes the Pople sets to ten significant figures and PySCF carries more, and the difference alone is worth 1e-7 -- enough to look like a bug in whichever code is being checked.
